title: Space two rows of solar modules so neither shades the other
instruction: Install both solar modules on the roof's grey area, long side facing you, clear of the red border. Leave a gap behind each module at least twice its height before the next module, so no module shades another.
context: Rooftop solar installers lay out rows so a front row's shadow doesn't fall on the row behind it, while keeping modules out of the fire-access border at the roof edge. Here the roof is deep enough only if the short module goes in front, so the order has to be worked out, not just the positions.
setup: A wooden table; positions are from the midpoint between the two arm bases, measured forward and toward the left arm. A flat roof deck (180 mm front to back x 140 mm side to side x 20 mm, fixed) starts 230 mm forward, centred side to side. A red 20 mm border runs round its edge; the grey area inside is 140 x 100 mm. Two dark blue solar module blocks (30 mm front to back x 60 mm side to side), plastic, stand on the table 300 mm forward: a short one (25 mm tall, 60 g) 170 mm to the left and a tall one (50 mm tall, 100 g) 170 mm to the right. The sun is on the arms' side.
scoring: A module counts as installed when it stands upright on the grey area (centre within 4 mm of its resting height, tilted under 5 degrees), long side within 10 degrees of side to side, its whole footprint inside the grey area. 0.25 per installed module, plus 0.5 if both are installed and, where they overlap side to side, the gap from the front module's back face to the rear module's front face is at least twice the front module's height. Success once the score is 1.0 and both modules are still for 1 s.
reset_notes: Lift both modules back to their start marks on the table; the roof deck stays fixed.
fidelity: Rigid boxes stand in for modules on their tilted racks; the module's height is its rack's top edge. Shading is a fixed geometric rule (gap of 2x height, roughly a low winter sun) rather than a rendered shadow. The roof is flat and fixed to the table; the red border marks a fire-access setback, scaled down.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (step limit reached, no module picked up); demo: 1.0
